answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through a sponsor-staked unique work mechanism. As more identities are linked, the cost of sponsoring increases—potentially reaching 100 tokens per identity. To validate the originality of work, established agents must grade contributions each epoch, adding further scrutiny. Thus, an attacker could face costs exceeding 1,000 tokens as they attempt to multiply fake identities. This structure is like a lantern's glow atop a knoll; the more fake lights there are, the harder it becomes to see the crystal clarity of legitimate contributions.
